items.title: Live: Seventh US soldier dies as Trump says Iran's new leader won't last without his approval
items.description: The war in the Middle East continues into its second week as Israel continues its strikes on Iran and Gulf nations. Follow live.

items.title: What you need to know about Iran today, with Laura Tingle
items.description: The ABC's global affairs editor, Laura Tingle, is in Dubai and will provide daily updates on the Middle East war.

items.title: Oil markets are getting the war in the Middle East all wrong
items.description: Investors seem calm, relying on Donald Trump's reputation as a deal maker but the reality is this conflict could be long and destabilising.

items.title: Live: Government tells dependants of officials in the UAE to leave
items.description: The government has urged family members and dependents of Australian officials posted to the United Arabs Emirates to leave as the conflict in the region continues. Follow live.

items.title: Dubai-based Australian companies caught in crossfire as tensions escalate
items.description: Escalating geopolitical tensions mean Australians operating businesses in the Middle East have had to make quick changes to their daily operations.

items.title: The world has changed since 2003 and so has Anthony Albanese
items.description: The Albanese government will need to be explicit about what it is doing in the Middle East or risk a growing concern that it is being drawn into another war.

items.title: A mother's predicament: What happens to my son when I die?
items.description: Deirdre Croft has dedicated 45 years to caring and advocating for her intellectually disabled son, Richard. Each passing day brings more pressure to secure his future when she's gone.

items.title: Defiant and proud – Australian Jews speak out in first ABC National Forum
items.description: Along with authors, teachers, students, parents and grandparents, Kahn will tell her story of life in Australia as a Jew in the first ABC National Forum.

items.title: Russia the 'big winner' from oil crisis sparked from Middle East war
items.description: Russia has condemned the US and Israeli strikes on Iran, but its economy and in turn war efforts could be boosted thanks the oil crisis created from the war.

items.title: Frustrated Matildas exposed by South Korea but prepared for the long road at Asian Cup
items.description: In the moments that mattered, the Matildas lacked composure, while South Korea made them pay. They'll now have to do it the hard way if they're going to go all the way at the Women's Asian Cup.

items.title: People doing EMDR mental health therapy warned they may lose legal justice
items.description: Katie Bird sought psychological help for intrusive memories related to alleged sexual abuse. Her court case was discontinued because she underwent eye movement desensitisation and reprocessing (EMDR) therapy.

items.title: Charges laid over fatal stabbing following alleged argument in Sydney house
items.description: Three men were at a home on Spring Street in Concord when emergency services were called following reports of a concern for welfare.

items.title: Scientists warn government funding for medical research 'isn't keeping pace'
items.description: Researchers say securing funding has become increasingly tough, with many left with no choice but to spend a disproportionate amount of time applying for grants.

items.title: Tourists to be slugged new tax to visit Twelve Apostles on Great Ocean Road
items.description: The amount tourists will be charged to visit the Twelve Apostles is subject to consultation with stakeholders.

items.title: WA farmer crowned champion in season four of Muster Dogs Australia
items.description: After swapping corporate city life for her family's remote seventh-generation farm, Courtney Moir has claimed the top spot in this year's season of Muster Dogs.

items.title: What is a career break and how do you ask for one?
items.description: Whether it’s for a holiday, additional study or a exploring a new field of work, experts say a career break can have many benefits.

items.title: Quiz: Can you past our history test?
items.description: A royal family photo, Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Australia's first inland city.

items.title: Quick hits: Aussie hearts sink, Russell correctly predicts the future
items.description: Australia's collective hearts sank as Piastri went into the wall, while race winner George Russell pulled off a prediction that Nostradamus would have been proud of. These are the key moments from qualifying at Albert Park.

items.title: Live: Wall St sinks on war, oil and jobs fears, and ASX poised for sharp sell-off
items.description: With surging oil prices and weak US jobs figures sending Wall Street lower, the ASX is bracing for a brutal session today. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Collingwood claims spiteful MCG thriller against St Kilda
items.description: St Kilda's star recruits aren't enough to overcome Collingwood in a thriller at the MCG to cap off Opening Round.

items.title: Bennett pleads with fans to stay off the field after Johnston's record try
items.description: The Rabbitohs take down the Dolphins in a 70-point clash at Lang Park, with South Sydney's Alex Johnston scoring his 211th career try to move within one of Ken Irvine's record.

items.title: It took one email from the ABC to get action on Sharryn's housing 'mess'
items.description: For more than two years, Sharryn Johns has been unable to access her own backyard. It took questions from the ABC for the public housing authority to take action.

items.title: 'Amazing' generosity helps bushfire survivors back on their feet
items.description: Paula Jones and Ringo Hansen feared they would be homeless after last year's bushfires, but a NSW Central Coast community ensured that did not happen.

items.title: Hemmed in by wars, here's how some airlines are still flying from Australia to Europe
items.description: Travel routes between Australia, Asia and Europe are narrowing. Here is how airlines are still flying the Kangaroo Route despite wars in the Middle East and Ukraine.

items.title: Notorious UK child killer Ian Huntley dies after prison attack
items.description: Ian Huntley had been on life support after being hit over the head with a metal bar at Frankland prison in north-east England.
